v1.feedback: The trumpet-bell flare mechanic is a genuine fanfare interpretation — periodic radius swell + brass color shift is conceptually on point. However, MeshBasicMaterial with no lighting makes the 3D tube form difficult to read between fanfare events; swap to MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhongMaterial with a subtle directional light so the calligraphic volume has depth cues at rest. The 11-second interval means you stare at a flat-shaded worm for a long opening stretch — drop the first fanfare to ~3s and vary subsequent intervals (7–13s) so the surprise lands faster and stays unpredictable. Consider tapering the bell flares asymmetrically (wider on the outward-facing lip) to sell the trumpet silhouette rather than symmetric bulges.

v2.feedback: The brass-bell flares are a genuine formal swerve — asymmetric trumpet blooms on an ink tube is a strong read of 'fanfare' and the gold-on-cream palette shift is restrained. Two issues: the bell flares are radius modulations on a per-frame rebuilt CatmullRomCurve3 tube, so at default camera distance (~17 units out) they may read as subtle wobbles rather than dramatic trumpet mouths — consider widening maxFlare or adding a slight emissive pulse on the brass segments so the swerve moment is unmissable. Second, the entire tube geometry is reallocated every frame (800-sample custom tube + normals); for a piece meant to run continuously, caching the base tube and only recalculating bell-affected cross-sections would cut GC pressure substantially and keep the animation smoother on mid-range GPUs.
